description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3” illustrates how the sparsity ratio of SDPA output varies across model layers for three conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with tick labels shown at regular intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.0 up to about 0.9 with tick labels at roughly 0.2 increments (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). A blue dashed line (legend: “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003”) stays very close to zero across all layers, starting near ~0.01 at layer 0 and approaching ~0.00 by the final layers. An orange dotted line (legend: “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126”) starts high near ~0.85 at layer 0, drops steeply over early layers (around ~0.40 by layer 2 and ~0.15 by about layer 5), then continues decreasing toward ~0.02–0.03 by around layers 12–16, with small late-layer fluctuations including a visible bump around layers ~20–22 (rising to roughly ~0.06–0.08) before ending near ~0.03–0.04. A green dash-dot line (legend: “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080”) also starts high near ~0.80 at layer 0, declines sharply to about ~0.28 by layer 1 and ~0.20 by layer 2, then decreases more gradually to around ~0.05 by about layer 7–8 and approaches ~0.01–0.02 in later layers, ending near ~0.01.
